title: Mapping Conditioning Contingencies in Real-World Scenarios
description: Classify behavioral modifications across positive/negative reinforcement and punishment contingencies.
problemStatement:
Operant conditioning distinguishes four fundamental contingencies based on whether a stimulus is added or removed, and whether target behavior increases or decreases.

### Scenarios to Analyze:
1. An automobile sounds a continuous irritating beeping chime until the driver fastens their seatbelt. (Fastening seatbelt increases).
2. A manager awards a $500 bonus to sales representatives who hit their monthly quota. (Sales efforts increase).
3. A student texting during class has their smartphone confiscated until the end of the semester. (Texting during class decreases).
4. A speeding driver receives a $250 traffic citation from a police officer. (Speeding decreases).

### Deliverables:
* Correctly categorize each scenario (Positive Reinforcement, Negative Reinforcement, Positive Punishment, or Negative Punishment).
* Identify the target behavior, the operational stimulus, and explain why Negative Reinforcement is frequently confused with Punishment.
hints: Hint 1: Reinforcement ALWAYS strengthens behavior; punishment ALWAYS weakens behavior.
Hint 2: Negative Reinforcement involves the removal of an unpleasant stimulus to encourage an action (e.g. fastening the seatbelt to stop the annoying beep).
